title: Egg Omelet with Cheese, Meat and Tomatoes

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet prepared with cheese, meat, tomatoes and a small amount of added fat is a nutritious dish popular for breakfast and light meals. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, while cheese, meat and tomatoes add flavor, texture, and additional nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: An omelet can be cooked in 5‑10 minutes, making it a quick meal option.
The combination of eggs and cheese increases the bioavailability of certain vitamins such as vitamin D and B12.
Tomatoes add lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable with heat.
Adding a modest amount of fat (oil or butter) improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins from eggs and cheese.
Different countries have their own styles: French "omelette soufflée", Japanese "tamago‑yaki", Spanish "tortilla".

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs and meat supply all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The omelet provides B2, B6 and B12, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Cheese and the added fat deliver monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Tomatoes contribute lycopene and vitamin C, helping combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Cheese is a good source of calcium and phosphorus, essential for strong bones.

items.title: Allergy to eggs or dairy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, cheese, or dairy fat.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese and processed meat can be salty; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Added fat and cheese increase the calorie count, so servings should be moderate.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; those with elevated cholesterol levels should consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, often with whole‑grain toast, fresh vegetables or herbs. Cook it in a skillet with a little oil, fold in cheese, diced meat and tomatoes near the end of cooking to retain flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a skillet or microwave, adding a splash of oil to prevent drying out.
